note: Every number below is copied from the quoted ledger row or report. A Python test (app/api/tests/test_learned_ledger.py) fails if a quoted number is not in its source. Lower is better for CRPS, log loss and Brier differences.

items.title: Averaging two models beat our best single model on points
items.claim: On the held-out 2025 season, averaging a sequence model with the recent-role model forecast points better than the recent-role model alone, and far better than the old production model. One logged touch of the holdout.

evidence.label: Points CRPS, average minus recent-role model
Points CRPS, average minus old production model

items.caveat: Points only. Rebounds, assists and threes improved by less than the -0.005 floor against the recent-role model. The attack review (T479) found it survives, but it is worse for players who play under 5 minutes (+0.0439 [+0.0360, +0.0518]). Moving it into production is Devin's decision.

items.title: Fixing the low end of points forecasts
items.claim: A mixture that gives short-minutes nights their own shape forecast the low end of points better than production, in the selection season and again in the report season. The holdout was not touched.
items.caveat: Rebounds, assists and threes gain less (for example rebounds 2024 -0.0029 [-0.0049, -0.0008]). Both seasons were used to design and report, so the live log is the clean test.

items.title: The injury report and recent minutes say who plays
items.claim: A model that reads the official injury report and the player's recent minutes predicts whether a player plays much better than the production minutes module, in both 2023 and 2024.

evidence.label: Chance-to-play log loss, new minus production, 2023
Chance-to-play log loss, new minus production, 2024

items.caveat: The attack review (T484) wounded this: the gain is real, but much of it is current-form information (recent minutes and missed games), not the report alone. Only players who appear in tonight's box score are scored. Not on the holdout.

items.title: Confirmed starters at T-30 improve points forecasts
items.claim: Thirty minutes before tip, knowing who actually starts improves points forecasts over the T-60 version. It is a different prediction time, so it says nothing about T-60.
items.caveat: The starter flag is a box-score proxy, so this is an upper bound. The red team (T166 notice) gives a range for points of -0.023 to -0.041. Threes (-0.002 to -0.004) fall below the practical floor. 2023 replication, descriptive: -0.0366. Not in production.

items.title: Re-calibrating at the posted line helps, but we still trail the market
items.claim: Mapping our probabilities onto what actually happens at the posted line improves them. After that they are still slightly worse than the market's own price.

evidence.label: Log loss, calibrated minus raw (Pinnacle lines)

items.caveat: Log loss after calibration 0.6882, a coin 0.6931, the market 0.6865: lower is better, so the market is still ahead. The ledger gives no interval for that last comparison. 2024 is partly exposed. The live 2026-27 log is the confirmatory test.

items.title: Five role columns helped points, but a safety check fired
items.claim: Adding five recent-role columns improved points forecasts on the 2025 holdout by more than expected. The frozen scrambled-label check also showed a gain, so the rule called it not a pass.

evidence.label: Points CRPS, with columns minus without
Same, with the training labels scrambled

items.caveat: A model should gain nothing when the labels are scrambled, so this gain may not come from the labels. Either chance or a real label-free effect. Final under the frozen rule; no rerun.

items.title: A longer training window helped in 2023 and not in 2024
items.claim: Adding older seasons to the training data helped points in 2023, when we had little data, and did nothing in 2024. The rule required both seasons.

evidence.label: Points CRPS, with older seasons minus without, 2023

items.caveat: The 2023 gain is a small-data effect, not a lasting one. No change was made.

items.title: When the team's top scorer is out, others' points shifted in 2023 only
items.claim: Modelling how minutes and points are redistributed when the leading scorer sits helped points in 2023. In 2024 the sign was the same but the interval crossed zero.

evidence.label: Points CRPS, structured minus role model, leader out, 2023

items.caveat: Not promoted. Assists showed nothing (-0.0022 and -0.0017). The live log is the next venue.

items.title: The mix of player types in a lineup matters, a little
items.claim: Which kinds of players share the floor explains a tiny, but not zero, share of how a lineup performs beyond the sum of its players.

evidence.label: Share of variation explained (R squared)
evidence.interval: none: permutation test, p 0.004 against a null R squared of 0.005

items.caveat: This row has no confidence interval, only a permutation test, so it is shown as a small real effect and nothing more. Practically negligible.

items.title: On game winners the market was better than our model
items.claim: In the 2025-26 replay, the price on Kalshi predicted who wins better than our model did. We make no claim of an edge on game winners.
items.caveat: Positive means the model is worse. Model Brier 0.2039, market 0.1975. Exploratory replay, described in docs/REPLAY_2025_26.md; it has no ledger row.
